classifications.rationale: This segment only recites statutory requirements and authority; it does not itself direct executive action or change any legal consequence.
classifications.evidence: Section 502(d)(1) of the Trade Act (19 U.S.C. 2462(d)(1)) provides that the President may withdraw, suspend, or limit the application of duty-free treatment

classifications.rationale: The President makes the statutory determination suspending Belarus's GSP benefits; the trade consequence follows from this present presidential act.
classifications.evidence: I have determined that it is appropriate to suspend Belarus's GSP benefits

classifications.rationale: The President states a determination that an HTS modification is appropriate but does not perform that modification in this segment.
classifications.evidence: I have determined that it is appropriate to modify general note 4(a)

classifications.rationale: The President presently makes the statutory high-income determination that triggers termination under the cited statute.
classifications.evidence: I have determined that Malta, French Polynesia, New Caledonia, and Slovenia meet the definition of a "high income" country

classifications.rationale: The President expressly terminates preferential tariff treatment as of a specified effective date.
classifications.evidence: I am terminating the preferential treatment under the GSP

classifications.rationale: The proclamation itself modifies the HTS country lists, thereby ending specified GSP treatment on the stated effective dates.
classifications.evidence: general note 4(a) of the HTS is modified by deleting "Belarus" from the list of independent countries
